title: The cumulative exports (merchandise & services) during April-September 2026-27 are estimated at US$ 476.20 Billion, as compared to US$ 418.31 Billion in April-September 2025-26, an estimated growth of 13.84%.
subtitle:
The cumulative value of merchandise exports during April-September 2026-27 was US$ 259.89 Billion, as compared to US$ 219.30 Billion during April-September 2025-26, registering a positive growth of 18.51%.
The cumulative Non-Petroleum exports in April-September 2026-27 valued at US$ 218.70 Billion registered an increase of 15.56% as compared to US$ 189.26 Billion in April-September 2025-26.
Major drivers of merchandise export growth in September 2026 include Electronic Goods, Petroleum Products, Organic & Inorganic Chemicals, Engineering Goods, Cotton Yarn/Fabs./Made-Ups, Handloom Products Etc.
Electronic Goods exports increased by 70.44% from US$ 3.11 Billion in September 2025 to US$ 5.31 Billion in September 2026.
Petroleum Products exports increased by 31.90% from US$ 4.71 Billion in September 2025 to US$ 6.22 Billion in September 2026.
Organic & Inorganic Chemicals exports increased by 24.21% from US$ 2.37 Billion in September 2025 to US$ 2.94 Billion in September 2026.
Engineering Goods exports increased by 20.91% from US$ 10.06 Billion in September 2025 to US$ 12.17 Billion in September 2026.
Cotton Yarn/Fabs./made-ups, Handloom Products exports increased by 20.76% from US$ 0.93 Billion in September 2025 to US$ 1.12 Billion in September 2026.
body_text:
India’s total exports (Merchandise and Services combined) for September 2026* are estimated at US$ 80.75 Billion, registering a positive growth of 10.99 percent vis-à-vis September 2025. Total imports (Merchandise and Services combined) for September 2026* are estimated at US$ 94.05 Billion, registering a growth of 8.19 percent vis-à-vis September 2025.

SERVICES TRADE
The estimated value of services export for September 2026* is US$ 36.35 Billion as compared to US$ 36.67 Billion in September 2025. The estimated value of services imports for September 2026* is US$ 19.44 Billion as compared to US$ 17.84 Billion in September 2025.
Fig 7: Services Trade during September 2026*
The estimated value of service exports during April-September 2026-27* is US$ 216.31 Billion as compared to US$ 199.02 Billion in April-September 2025-26. The estimated value of service imports during April-September 2026-27* is US$ 113.60 Billion as compared to US$ 100.24 Billion in April-September 2025-26. The services trade surplus for April-September 2026-27* is US$ 102.71 Billion as compared to US$ 98.77 Billion in April-September 2025-26.

(11.23%), Coffee (10.17%), Marine Products (8.79%), Oil Seeds (5.1%), Leather & Leather Products (4.79%), Drugs & Pharmaceuticals (4.68%), Rice (4.21%), and Spices (4.01%) recorded positive growth during September 2026 over the corresponding month of last year. Imports of Project Goods (-86.85%), Gold (-81.27%), Silver (-49.11%), Fertilisers, Crude & Manufactured (-22.18%), Newsprint (-9.1%), Iron & Steel (-5.33%), Wood & Wood Products (-3.41%), and Medcnl. & Pharmaceutical Products (-0.19%) recorded negative growth during September 2026 over the corresponding month of last year. Services exports are estimated to grow by 8.69 percent during April-September 2026-27* over April-September 2025-26. Top 5 export destinations, in terms of change in value, exhibiting positive growth in September 2026 vis a vis September 2025 are U S A (47.99%), Singapore (169.16%), Malaysia (119.69%), Egypt A Rp (90.09%), and China P Rp (24.05%). Top 5 export destinations, in terms of change in value, exhibiting positive growth in April-September 2026-27 vis a vis April-September 2025-26 are Singapore (103.05%), U S A (11.11%), China P Rp (36.07%), Tanzania Rep (122.51%), and Malaysia (82.85%). Top 5 import sources, in terms of change in value, exhibiting growth in September 2026 vis a vis September 2025 are China P Rp (31.52%), Oman (331.82%), Russia (25.63%), Korea Rp (52.93%), and Singapore (36.44%) Top 5 import sources, in terms of change in value, exhibiting growth in April-September 2026-27 vis a vis April-September 2025-26 are China P Rp (27.82%), Russia (51.97%), Oman (210.9%), U S A (25.98%), and Brazil (143.13%).
